data.method: Parsed every changed JSON record; compared all four locked titles and spoken bodies byte-for-text against the approved copy; ran the reusable standalone Shorts contract directly on STANDALONE-SCRIPTS-V3.json; ran eight direct-contract tests, eight eval-package Shorts tests and the complete 23-test studio suite; compiled every changed Python module; ran git diff whitespace checks; validated the oe-video-direction skill package; appended decision and owner-acceptance records only through decision_log.py; and validated the EP007 hash chain plus current-event evidence bindings.
data.scope: The four-script V3 lock, the reusable companion-Short contract, future Originate derivation schema, archived-brief cutting fallback, active rubric/docs, and the OE video-direction method and precedent index. The exact V3 manifest passes as four direct records with cold-viewer context, exact hook/payoff/closing phrases in correct order, a declared complete narrow payoff and no required episode bridge.
data.limitations: Automation validates declared fields, exact-copy relationships, ordering and obvious CTA deferral; it cannot prove that a finished performance is persuasive or that a cold viewer experiences the payoff as useful. Claim-linked Content OS clearance, jurisdiction-specific legal review, visual direction, narration, avatar performance, caption timing, phone playback with sound, render, Related Video target, release, publication and provider spend remain pending or unauthorized. The full 310-event EP007 chain is structurally valid, but its evidence audit still reports pre-existing stale historical bindings unrelated to these three V6 events. Content OS consumes a commit-pinned OE standard, so the external release gate cannot use this local rubric revision until the repo change is committed and its pin is refreshed.
